summary:
AqroVision is an interactive precision agriculture and agrometeorological monitoring dashboard. Integrating Leaflet satellite mapping, NASA POWER Earth observation telemetry, and Open-Meteo forecasting, the platform features field boundary polygon drawing, multi-depth soil moisture tracking (surface, root zone, profile), evapotranspiration (modeling, automated drought and heat stress risk indices, an AI crop advisory system, and an intelligent farming assistant.

How It Addresses the Challenge:
Small-to-medium farmers often struggle with crop loss and inefficient resource allocation due to climate unpredictability and the high expense of physical in-ground sensors. AqroVision eliminates guesswork by democratizing satellite remote-sensing data into free, field-specific intelligence. By analyzing root-zone moisture dynamics alongside predictive rainfall and evaporation data, it delivers clear, actionable irrigation advisories and early warning alerts before stress damages crops.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

AqroVision is an end-to-end precision agrometeorological platform that translates global Earth observation satellite data into hyper-local, field-level agricultural intelligence:

  1. Geospatial Field Mapping:
    Using an interactive Leaflet.js interface with high-resolution satellite imagery (Esri, Google Satellite, OpenStreetMap), farmers can locate their land via Nominatim geocoding or GPS, click a point, or draw custom polygon boundaries. The platform automatically calculates spherical field area (in hectares) and boundary perimeters using Haversine spherical projection formulas.
  2. Multi-Source Data Ingestion & Synthesis:
    Upon selecting a field, AqroVision queries multiple real-time scientific APIs concurrently:
    • NASA POWER API: Extracts multi-depth soil moisture across three layers—Surface (0–5 cm0\text{--}5\text{ cm}0–5 cm), Root Zone (0–100 cm0\text{--}100\text{ cm}0–100 cm), and Soil Profile—along with surface temperature, solar radiation, humidity, and historical rainfall.
    • ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0: Fetches physical and chemical soil profiles (clay, silt, sand percentages, pHH2O\text{pH}_{\text{H}_2\text{O}}pHH2​O​, and Soil Organic Carbon / SOC) at varying depths.
    • Open-Meteo & Elevation APIs: Provides 7-day predictive weather forecasting, hourly temperatures, and topographic altitude.
    • NASA GIBS WMTS: Overlays live satellite rasters, including MODIS NDVI (vegetation health), SMAP (root-zone moisture), MODIS Land Surface Temperature, and IMERG precipitation.
  3. Agronomic Modeling & Risk Analytics:
    • Evapotranspiration (ET0\text{ET}_0ET0​): Calculates daily reference evapotranspiration using the FAO-56 Hargreaves Radiation Model, accounting for solar declination, extraterrestrial radiation (RaR_aRa​), and thermal ranges.
    • Atmospheric Demand: Computes Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD) in kilopascals via Tetens' saturation vapor pressure equations.
    • Risk Scoring: Generates automated indices for Drought Risk (derived from root-zone moisture deficit), Heat Stress (Tmax⁡>25∘CT_{\max} > 25^\circ\text{C}Tmax​>25∘C thresholds), and Water Deficit (comparing forecasted rain to cumulative ET0\text{ET}_0ET0​).
  4. Actionable Recommendations & Interactive AI:
    • Matches local soil texture (classified using USDA standards) and climate conditions against an agronomic matrix to recommend optimal crops, vegetables, and fruits.
    • Features an integrated AgroChat Assistant loaded with the field's live data context to provide specific guidance on planting, pest prevention, and irrigation.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Zero Hardware Investment: Eliminates the need for expensive in-ground soil moisture probes, telemetry stations, or ongoing sensor maintenance costs.
  • Data-Driven Water Conservation: Prevents both under-irrigation and wasteful over-irrigation by balancing root-zone depletion against forecasted rain and evapotranspiration.
  • Proactive Risk Mitigation: Delivers early alerts for impending droughts, heat waves, and water stress before visible crop wilting occurs.
  • Scientific Crop Selection: Prevents planting failures by evaluating real physical soil characteristics (salinity, pH, soil texture) and regional elevation rather than relying on guesswork.
  • Digital Farm Records & Reporting: Allows farmers to save fields, record dated field observations/notes, and generate printable diagnostic agronomic field reports.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Empowering Small & Medium Family Farms: High-tech precision farming is typically restricted to large agribusinesses with enterprise budgets. AqroVision democratizes remote-sensing tools for smallholders at zero cost.
  • Climate Resilience & Food Security: In arid and semi-arid agricultural zones (such as the Kura-Araz basin and Mediterranean climates), water scarcity and shifting rainfall patterns threaten yields. AqroVision equips farmers with climate-adaptive intelligence to maintain food production stability.
  • Environmental Sustainability: Optimizes groundwater extraction, protects aquifers from over-pumping, and minimizes soil salinization and nutrient runoff caused by excessive irrigation.

4. Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software used

  • Languages: Native JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5 (semantic markup, WAI-ARIA accessibility), and CSS3 (custom design tokens, Flexbox/Grid).
  • Libraries & Mapping Engines:
    • Leaflet.js (v1.9.4): Interactive geospatial vector drawing, tile layer controls, and coordinate tracking.
    • Chart.js (v4.4.1): Dual-axis responsive line and bar charts tracking historical soil moisture, precipitation, and thermal trends.
  • Satellite & Agrometeorological Data Services:
    • NASA POWER API (Agroclimatology daily telemetry)
    • NASA GIBS WMTS (MODIS NDVI, SMAP L4, MODIS LST, IMERG, VIIRS)
    • ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 REST API (Global soil physical/chemical properties)
    • Open-Meteo Weather & Elevation APIs
    • Nominatim & BigDataCloud APIs (Forward and reverse geocoding)
  • Data Persistence: Client-side HTML5 Web Storage (LocalStorage) for user accounts, saved polygon boundaries, and field notes.
  • Hardware Compatibility: Completely hardware-agnostic. Runs in any modern web browser across mobile smartphones, tablets, and desktop workstations without requiring local installation.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Virtual Soil Sensing via Data Fusion: Instead of relying on a single data feed, the application fuses satellite telemetry (NASA), global digital soil mapping (ISRIC), and predictive meteorology (Open-Meteo) into a cohesive digital twin of the farmer's soil profile.
  • Interactive "What-If" Soil Simulator: Farmers can toggle a simulation mode to test management actions (e.g., adding lime/gypsum to modify soil pH, incorporating compost to boost organic matter, or adjusting irrigation methods) and see real-time updates to crop suitability scores.
  • Context-Injected Agronomic AI: Rather than an isolated generic chatbot, the AgroChat Drawer automatically inspects the currently selected field's soil texture, root moisture, upcoming precipitation, and heat index to deliver farm-specific advisory answers.
  • Modern Agronomic Glassmorphism Design: Blends aesthetic glassmorphism (translucent panels, ambient gradients) with high-contrast, outdoor-readable UI elements and instant Light/Dark mode switching designed for outdoor sunlight legibility.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Rural Connectivity & Network Latency: Field conditions often suffer from unstable cellular data. The system implements request timeouts via AbortController, parallel asynchronous fetching (Promise.allSettled), client-side caching (S.soilCache), and forward-fill algorithms to bridge data gaps without crashing.
  • Language & Digital Literacy Barriers: Built with an embedded trilingual dictionary (English, Azerbaijani, and Russian) and intuitive visual indicators (color-coded danger badges, weather iconography, and progress bars) so farmers can assess conditions at a glance without deciphering raw telemetry tables.
  • Scientific Rigor: Implemented validated international standards, including FAO-56 Hargreaves evapotranspiration calculations, the USDA Soil Texture Triangle, and Tetens' equation for atmospheric vapor pressure deficit.
  • Data Privacy & Zero Friction: No complex cloud database setup or invasive tracking is required; farmer data (field boundaries, custom notes) stays stored securely in the farmer's own browser storage.
